newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French September bond futures ended slightly higher on Wednesday in a market which lacked conviction with investors waiting for Monday's publication of an audit into France's public finances, dealers said.
A slightly weaker than expected U.S. June CPI figure allowed the notionnel to test resistance at 130.32 but the contract failed to break through.

"The figures were neutral and did not allow a lot," said a dealer, adding the market remained boxed in on worries about European monetary union with worries that France was set to miss on the deficit criteria in the Maastricht treaty.

Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn said on Wednesday after the regular cabinet meeting that he hoped the deficit would be as low as possible. Junior budget minister Christian Sautter suggested it could be slightly over 3.5 percent of GDP.
Prime Minister Lionel Jospin will meet ministers on Thursday to review measures designed to curb the budget deficit ahead of the release on Monday of an audit of public finances.

Many expect it to target a deficit level of around 3.3 percent of GDP, above the 3.0 percent forecast by the previous centre-right government, but below the 3.5 percent or so expected to be estimated by the audit.
Trautmann declined comment on a report in Le Monde that the government planned a one-year rise in corporate taxation to buckle the budget.

"The big problem is the mark/dollar rate which is preventing the French market from rising. If the mark continues to deteriorate against the dollar there could be an upset in the German market and by contagion in France," a dealer said.

The franc, also weaker against the dollar while keeping up with the mark, could lose some ground towards the July 21 publication date for the budget audit. "A deficit of more than 3.5 percent would have a damaging effect," a trader said.
The Bank of France's monetary policy council is meeting on Thursday. It is not expected to change its rates.
In the cash market, the 5.50 percent OAT due in 2007 was trading at 100.42 for a yield of 5.44 percent, down from 5.48 on Tuesday. The yield gap with bunds widened to 16 points from 14 points.
On the money market, call money remained unchanged at 3-1/8 3-1/4 percent while the three-month rate was two basis points lower at 3.28-3.38 percent.

The government paid 90.9 billion francs on Wednesday to re-imburse co-called Balladur bonds held by the public. Dealers said this did not create additional demand in the bond market. A great number of special savings instruments have been created to attract the money and a large part is expected to be invested in the share market.
The Finance Ministry said that the budget deficit at the end of May stood at 241.3 billion francs. This figure compares to a deficit of 253.5 billion at the end of May 1996.
France will sell between 19 and 21 billion francs and 600 to 800 million ecus of 4.50 percent, July 2002 BTANs on Thursday.
France is selling for the first time on Thursday BTANs with the same characteristics in francs and ecus to make them easily interchangeable after the launch of the euro in 1999.
